properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a path citation carries no repository because a location is a free string anchored to an IMPLICIT root (the folder the store is opened in) that no schema field, design_identity or export records — so a move or archive re-anchors every relative path silently, and a moved design reads an unchanged file as missing_artifact; most citations are prose, which a field on Artifact would not reach
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on Anthony's word, 2026-09-28, on art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27, the gap of 2026-09-27 (session 62995724, moving the project to flo2.io) and wish #48.

① OBSERVED, verbatim: "Hundreds of nodes cite `docs/...` / `scripts/...` paths; when the repo holding them was archived, nothing in the graph could say which repo a path belongs to." The reporter recorded the archive in a Decision and in AGENTS.md instead. Expected: a reader can follow a citation without knowing the history. NOT affected: URI locations, which name their host.

② PRECEDENT, searched ("repository qualifier", "relocation", "archived repo", "sibling repo"). dec:idea-a-design-apart-from-its-code-knows-where-its-implementation-is (need accepted 2026-09-25, mechanism unchosen; option (a) "every artifact names its repository", (b) "the design names its implementations once"). req:the-design-knows-where-each-implementation-is and req:the-design-says-who-can-reach-each-artifact are both proposed and unscheduled. No prior finding had measured the missing anchor itself.

③ CANDIDATES:
 A: a location is relative to an IMPLICIT root that nothing in the design records.
 B: it is a prose problem. The "hundreds" are statement text, which no structured field reaches.
 C: the design CAN say it (an Artifact per repo, external_dependency, design_identity's label), and the reporter did not use it.
 D (outside the suspect component, the move procedure): the import that moved the design dropped an anchor that had been recorded.
 E: the observation is wrong, and something does carry a repository.

④ WHAT WOULD REFUTE EACH: A and D are separated by whether ANY record of the root exists before a move. E is refuted by a schema and export census. B is weighed by counting prose citations against structured locations. C is refuted if no existing field ties a path to a repository.

⑤ TAKEN:
 · Schema (schema/build.yaml, core.yaml): Artifact.location is a free string ("File path, URI, content-hash, or physical identifier"). No property named repository, root, remote or checkout exists on ANY node type. Fragment has no location at all (reflow2's 389: title, provenance, status, fragment_type, content_ref, note_kind). In reflow2's own export, across 5,661 nodes the only repo-ish key is one ChangeEvent's `commits`, and no edge property names a repo. E REFUTED.
 · Resolution: relative to the tree root, which is the folder the store's .reflow2/ sits in (--tree-root overrides; a registry or hosted server has none and answers `no_tree`). design_identity on a scratch design carries graph_id, label (the folder's name), minted_by and origin, with no root. The export carries none either. A HOLDS: before any move, no record of the anchor exists, so D is not a separate cause.
 · A move, measured on 0.72.0: the scratch design was exported and imported into another folder. design_identity's label became the NEW folder's name and origin became `adopted`; nothing of the old root survived. `docs/note.md`, unchanged in its own repo, then read missing_artifact: a relocation reported as a deletion.
 · C: external_dependency links designs, not repositories, and the label is a folder name reassigned on import. REFUTED as a structural way to say it.
 · Counts, reflow2's own design (docs/design/reflow2.json, read-only): 472 Artifacts. 471 are relative (458 resolve on disk; 13 are absent: 12 retired feedback copies and getting-started/skills/log-issue/SKILL.md), 1 is a URI, 0 are absolute, 0 are `../`. In prose, 1,130 non-Artifact nodes cite 1,682 relative repo paths (docs/, tools/, crates/, scripts/, src/ …), and only 7 nodes name a repository in a path. B HOLDS AS A REFINEMENT: prose citations outnumber structured locations about 3.6 to 1.

⑥ CLASS: the same as fact:root-cause-one-root-derived-from-the-stores-folder-leaves-a-sibling-repo-unmeasured-2026-09-28. DESIGN AND CODE WERE ASSUMED TO SHARE ONE ROOT, SO A PATH NEVER HAD TO SAY WHICH. req:persistence supplied the anchor implicitly, because the design sat inside the repo it described. It was dropped 2026-09-25, and nothing took its place in the schema, identity or export. #609 does not change this: the pointer runs code → design and names designs, not where their paths are anchored. The hosted door makes it sharper: the server has no root, so every relative path there is anchored to nothing.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSION: HELD. Nothing in the graph says which repository a path belongs to, and an archive or move re-anchors every relative citation silently. REFINED: most citations are prose, so a field on Artifact reaches only a minority of them.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE (no fix in this triage). A class-pinning test would assert: after export → import into a different folder or onto a server, every location still says which tree it is anchored to; an artifact unchanged in its own repository is never reported missing_artifact after the move; and a location reads back with its repository without consulting the process's cwd or store path.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. The storyflow design's own counts on flo2 were not read (its tools are out of bounds for this triage). Whether flo2's hosted import records anything about the source folder was not checked (flo2's gateway not read). The prose-citation regex is approximate.
